cards.b: give the full diagnosis — side + extent + "cleft lip" (e.g. left unilateral complete cleft lip). Closed mouth → describe the lip only; open mouth with the palate visible → lip + palate. Don't comment on the palate unless it is shown.
cosmetic/psychosocial is the main problem; feeding mildly affected (poor seal — usually managed with appropriate nipples); speech and hearing not significantly affected.

before ~3 months — avoid unnecessary very early surgery, let the infant grow and identify other problems; after ~6 months — the child becomes mobile and moves to solids, so post-op care is harder. Delayed repair can still give a similar result.

reconstruct the lip in layers — mucosa, orbicularis oris, skin; partial correction of the nasal deformity. Definitive rhinoplasty is postponed — aggressive early rhinoplasty scars and interferes with nasal/facial growth.
